班杜裡亞為撥弦發聲，現代西班牙版有六對十二弦，每對同度，音高以四度排列；低四弦較: The bandurria sounds by plucking; the modern Spanish version has six pairs, twelve strings, each pair in unison and tuned in fourths; the bottom four strings are a minor third above a standard guitar and the top two a perfect fourth above. Its timbre is close to the mandolin and the bandola, but the fourteen-string Philippine version is lower in pitch, and South American versions mostly have four courses with tuning close to the guitar.

班杜裡亞琴主要用於西班牙民間音樂，也出現在阿利坎特省希霍納兒童喪禮的伴奏，以及十: The bandurria is used mainly in Spanish folk music, and also accompanied children's funerals in Sijena, Alicante province, and the zapateo dance, which tobacco growers from the Canary Islands brought in before the end of the 19th century. In the Philippines it is common in folk songs and is part of the plucked-string rondalla; in Peru and Bolivia there are four-course variants, and in Lima it was played in duet with the harp, and it is still used for the Peruvian waltz or criollo waltz. The Scottish folk group the Corries trio and its successor the Corries choir have also used it.
班杜裡亞琴為撥弦魯特琴類，基本操作先依地區版本確認弦組與調音：西班牙現代型十二弦: The bandurria is a plucked lute; first establish, for the regional version, the courses and the tuning — the modern Spanish type has twelve strings in six unison pairs, tuned in fourths from low to high; the Philippine type has fourteen strings and sixteen frets and is tuned lower than the Spanish; the South American type commonly has four courses tuned close to the guitar. It sounds when the strings are plucked, and a beginner can start with the courses, the tuning and the paired unisons, then go on to Spanish folk music, Philippine plucked ensembles and Peruvian waltz accompaniment.
班杜裡亞琴為西班牙撥弦魯特琴類樂器。中世紀原為三弦，文藝復興增為四弦，巴洛克時期: The bandurria is a Spanish plucked lute. In the Middle Ages it had three strings; the Renaissance raised it to four; in the Baroque it became five pairs, ten strings. Before the 18th century the back was round and arched; in the 18th century it turned to a flat back with five courses tuned in fourths; the modern instrument has six pairs, twelve strings. Juan Ruiz first mentions a related name in the 14th century, and in 1555 Juan Bermudo described the three-string type. It later appears in former Spanish colonies such as the Philippines, Peru and Bolivia, and Roy Williamson used it in Scottish folk music.
班杜里亞琴是源自西班牙的撥弦弦鳴樂器，分類編號321.321，屬魯特琴類。現代型: The bandurria is a plucked chordophone from Spain, classification number 321.321, in the lute family. The modern type has a flat back and twelve strings in six pairs tuned in fourths, close to the mandolin and bandola. It is used mainly in Spanish folk music and also in former Spanish colonies: in the Philippines it joins plucked ensembles, and in Lima it was played in duet with the harp and accompanies the Peruvian waltz.
